stories.title: AGIBOT shows a third-generation humanoid hardware platform and a new robot foundation model at its Innovation Day in Shanghai
paragraphs: Chinese humanoid robot maker AGIBOT held its AGIBOT Innovation Day 2026 at the Shanghai World Expo Center on Oct. 29, 2026, the company said in posts on its official X account. AGIBOT said it introduced Worken, which it describes as a proposed framework for measuring the productive work robots perform in real-world environments, looking beyond deployment numbers to how autonomously and effectively they complete tasks.

According to AGIBOT, the event also showcased AHA3, its third-generation humanoid hardware architecture and first commercial "Three Intelligences in One" hardware platform; AGILE, which the company describes as advances in motion intelligence including self-evolving agent capabilities; and a preview of GO-3, its next-generation embodied AI foundation model.

The company also listed WITA-Omni 1.0, a multimodal foundation model for human-robot interaction; G2 Max, an industrial robot designed for demanding material-handling tasks in manufacturing and logistics; and Link-U OS 1.0, an operating system for embodied AI that AGIBOT says was officially released at the event. AGIBOT's posts did not give prices or availability dates for the new hardware.

stories.title: ANYbotics starts delivering ANYmal X, a four-legged inspection robot certified for explosive atmospheres
paragraphs: Swiss robotics company ANYbotics launched ANYmal X on Oct. 27, 2026, and began delivering it to customers, The Robot Report reports. The company calls the four-legged robot "the world's first legged inspection robot for explosive atmospheres," designed to meet strict safety standards in oil, gas and chemical plants and to run routine autonomous inspections in places that are dangerous for people.

According to ANYbotics, every device used in hazardous zones must be certified as unable to ignite a flammable atmosphere, even when something fails, and ANYmal X was built to comply with the ATEX standard in Europe and IECEx globally. The company said the robot's AI computer and inspection equipment sit in sealed, nitrogen-filled chambers, its 12 leg actuators and battery are protected by flameproof casings, its feet are conductive for grounding, and automatic cutoffs monitor temperature. CEO Péter Fankhauser said four years of engineering and more than 10 patents went into the robot.

The Robot Report says ANYmal X carries thermal, visual, acoustic and gas sensors to detect overheating, leaks, abnormal noise and equipment wear, and runs on ANYbotics' Shift software, which connects findings to plant maintenance systems including SAP, Yokogawa and SLB. Since 2023, companies including BP, Equinor, Shell, PETRONAS, Petrobras, BASF and SLB have tested the robot on hundreds of onshore and offshore missions through an early access program, the company said.

ANYbotics, a 2016 spinout of ETH Zurich, says it has raised more than $150 million and has about 200 employees in Zurich, San Francisco and Barcelona. The robot and its software will be shown publicly for the first time at the ADIPEC 2026 energy conference by ANYbotics, SLB and Kuwait Oil Co., according to the article.

stories.title: North American robot orders jumped 24.8% in the third quarter of 2026, the strongest quarter of the year, A3 says
paragraphs: North American companies ordered 10,989 robots valued at $723.5 million in the third quarter of 2026, according to data from the Association for Advancing Automation (A3) reported by The Robot Report on Oct. 28, 2026. That is an increase of 24.8% in units and 26.1% in value compared with the third quarter of 2025, and A3 said it was the strongest quarter of the year so far. Orders for the first nine months of 2026 reached 28,984 robots worth about $1.89 billion, up 9.6% in units.

A3 said automotive OEM orders, which fell in the first half of the year, grew 7.5% in the third quarter, though they remain 17% below last year's level through September. Orders from automotive component suppliers rose 90.4%. Among other industries, A3 reported unit increases of 97.6% in semiconductors and electronics/photonics, 67.7% in plastics and rubber, 38.7% in life sciences, pharmaceutical and biomedical, and 37.0% in metals, while food and consumer goods orders fell 23.7%.

Collaborative robots, designed to work alongside people, also grew: companies ordered 1,831 of them worth $63.8 million in the quarter, about 56% more units than a year earlier, making up 16.7% of all robot units ordered, A3 said. "What stands out in the third quarter is not simply the magnitude of the growth, but how broadly it was distributed across the market," said Alex Shikany, executive vice president at A3.

A3 linked the growth in electronics to investment in U.S. semiconductor manufacturing and noted that higher input costs, trade uncertainty and the timing of large manufacturing projects remain factors to watch.
